description: Supergene chalcocite enrichment blanket at the (paleo)water table above an exposed porphyry, under a leached, hematitic cap.
notes: A child of deeptime:porphyry_cu_mo_au: its tonnage and grade come from the parent (copper conserved: the leached column's copper, concentrated k-fold at k × the hypogene grade), not from sizing, which only documents the ranges.

USGS SIR 2010-5070-B (John et al. 2010): enrichment up to 3× in the Andes (p. 66, restating Sillitoe 2005), up to ~8× in the south-western US; enriched sulfide ore 0.4–1.7 % Cu (pp. 4, 65); enriched zone seldom thicker than 200 m (p. 25); blankets form at the top of the water table (p. 120); rainfall of 10 cm/yr or more (p. 68, one Andean stage); the same source says enrichment happens from tropical to hyper-arid climates, so the precip lower bound is 0 (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-02,

; it was 100 mm/yr). Supergene activity lasted at least 0.4–6.2 Myr per deposit (Sillitoe & McKee 1996, USGS record 70018070); the plan's 0.5 Myr minimum (Sillitoe 2005) is used. See crates/deeptime-core/data/usgs/supergene_cu.json.
Enrichment applies to copper only: Mo, Au and Ag enrichment is not documented (SIR 2010-5070-B).

PLACEHOLDERS (no USGS grade–tonnage model exists for blankets): tonnage_mt 10 / 100 / 1500 (the text gives 'tens of Mt' to more than 1.5 Gt), cu_pct p50 0.8 inside the 0.4–1.7 % range, ore_density_t_m3 2.7, density_per_1e5km2 and clustering (unused by a child), leach_depth_m and max_top_depth_m 300 ('several hundred m' of leached cap).

Design values: min_water_table_m 50, precip upper bound 1500 mm (hot semi-arid to pluvial, not quantified), max_erosion_m_myr 50 (erosion must not outpace enrichment), zoning split and densities, the blanket's aspect.
